Half (a) is already recorded SATISFIED in the observation (all eleven field values read back from the live /api/bot/config on 2026-08-30, with /api/diag/version showing git_sha 892c9a2c), so re-probing it would test a settled question. This looks for a CLOSED trade that is real-money, on one of the nine shipped e35 legs, whose pnlProvenance is measured or estimated (clears_when explicitly rules out fabricated and unverified), and — the word clears_when calls 'the whole criterion' — OPENED AFTER the deploy rather than merely closed after it. The boundary 2026-08-30T14:05:00+00:00 is not the commit time: it is the instant the observation records half (a) as MEASURED true on the running trader, so a matching trade demonstrably opened under config confirmed live. It is conservative by construction — it may exclude a qualifying trade opened slightly earlier, which errs toward under-reporting, the safe direction for a criterion that must not be cleared spuriously. `openedAt` is compared lexicographically, which is chronological ONLY because the route serves a +00:00 offset (measured); a switch to a 'Z' suffix would silently break it, and the positive control is what would catch that. The control is the leg-name set itself, matching 40 of 200 rows on 2026-08-31 — so a renamed leg turns this into could_not_look rather than a permanent quiet negative.
results.is_not: A pass does NOT establish that the trade was closed BY THE STRATEGY. clears_when forbids grading the exit off exit_reason alone, and the row's own near-miss is the proof: trade 4904 read 'reconciler_filled' for what was an OPERATOR FLATTEN. No field on this route separates a strategy exit from an operator action, so that judgement stays a session's. Nor does a pass establish BROKER TRUTH, which clears_when asks for: pnlProvenance grades how THIS ROW's number was derived, while journalTrust grades whether the ACCOUNT reconciles with the venue wallet at all, and they are different questions — a 'measured' row on a 'known_divergent' account is exactly that gap, and bybit_2 is such an account. Finally it cannot tell whether the trade exercised the CHANGED geometry: a trade on ada_pullback_2h or trend_donchian_xrp_4h that closed on its stop says nothing about the tp_r 50->3/4 change those two legs received, which is the part of the ship the row most wants looked at. Read the matching row, then read PB-20260830-XRP-4H-FIRST-CLOSE-UNDER-NEW-BRACKET-UNVERIFIED, before grading any first close.

results.checks: Looks for a gpu-burst-train.yml run whose logs carry the preflight step at all, over the last 20 runs. ⚠️ THE REASON THIS ROW CARRIED FOR HAVING NO PROBE WAS A CATEGORY ERROR, which is why it now has one: it said a scheduled probe 'cannot produce that without FIRING a GPU job, which spends real budget'. True about FIRING and irrelevant to PROBING — NO probe in this family produces the event it watches (pairs_soak does not open a pair; arbitration_fanout_soak does not route an order). Conflating producing an observation with observing it turned a buildable probe into a declared impossibility. This fires no job, spends nothing, and only reads.
results.is_not: ⚠️ A PASS HERE IS THE WEAKEST IN THE FAMILY AND MUST NOT CLEAR THE ROW ON ITS OWN. clears_when demands the preflight be OBSERVED MAKING A DECISION — refusing on budget or admitting — and explicitly rules out a dry run. This cannot separate those: with GPU_BURST_ARMED != 1 the workflow runs a DRY PREFLIGHT ONLY, and its log carries the same step name as an armed run. So a pass means 'a run exists that reached the preflight step', and a session must read that run's own output to see whether it was armed and what it decided. The literal is deliberately the step name rather than a decision string, because no decision string has ever been observed in a real run — inventing one would be a predicate matching nothing while looking precise. Tighten it to the real decision line the first time an armed run happens. Since the event never occurs spontaneously, a FAIL here means 'nobody has fired one', not 'the gate is broken'.

results.checks: BOTH halves, in the two DIFFERENT workflows that print them, because clears_when requires both and a pass on one half is the over-read this family exists to prevent. (a) `session-brief: verdict=inherited` in a guards.yml run — emitted only by render_session_brief.py's inherited branch, so its presence IS the diff-scoping path having been taken on a real PR. (b) `commit-to-main: stale-branch refresh ->` in a due-list.yml run — the composite action prints it with the resulting state, proving the automation branch is on the new code path at all. Each group is scanned over the last 20 runs and EVERY group must hit. The positive control `session-brief:` appears in essentially every guards run, so a workflow rename, an expired log or a revoked token becomes could_not_look instead of a permanent quiet negative.
results.is_not: A pass does NOT establish that half (a) came from a PR that genuinely did not touch the registers — the log line does not carry the diff, and `inherited` is explicitly NOT 'the brief is fine', it is 'this PR did not break it'. Nor does it tell which of `-> refreshed` and `-> not_needed_up_to_date` half (b) printed; clears_when accepts either, but they mean different things and a session grading the mechanism should read which. ⚠️ THIS READER HAS NEVER RUN AGAINST THE REAL ACTIONS API: api.github.com is intercepted at HTTP 403 from a Claude Code on the web sandbox, so its controls run against a fake server and its FIRST scheduled run is its real verification. That is safe only because a broken reader here reports could_not_run, never fail — if this row shows could_not_run after the probes workflow has run, suspect the reader before the mechanism. Finally, clears_when's own escape hatch stands: a run printing `verdict=base_unreadable` is a FINDING about the ref, not evidence for this row, and no probe makes that call.
